title: Sketch a road
description: Draw a new road on the open hillside in one stroke, finish the sketch and find the road you created.

setup.goal: Sketch a new road in one stroke and find it as the active road.
audience: Forest road designers new to PGMaps
access: None: the lesson opens the synthetic training project, which needs no sign-in and no data download.
setup.startingScreen: The road designer on the Hillside access training project, zoomed to a road-free patch of the hillside.
limitations: The readings are those of the synthetic training terrain and the Hillside access roads as shipped.

check.description: the sketch tool is in hand

overlay.title: Pick up the sketch tool
overlay.body: Select Sketch a road. The panel above the plan says when the tool is ready.

check.description: the project holds a third road

overlay.title: Draw the road in one stroke
overlay.body: Press on the open hillside near the lower left and drag up to the right in one gentle S-curve, then let go. Start away from the existing roads: a stroke that touches a road’s end extends that road instead. The stroke becomes editable points, with curves fitted where the minimum radius allows.

check.description: the sketch tool is put down

overlay.title: Put the tool down
overlay.body: Select Done sketching to inspect the result. To extend the road first, draw another stroke that meets its end.

overlay.title: Find the new road
overlay.body: Road name reads Sketched road 3: the new road is the active one. The number counts the roads already in the project.
